ns2:group.ns2:description:
Does native English sound too fast to understand? This daily listening practice will help you get used to the natural speed and rhythm of spoken English.
In this video, you'll listen to practical, slightly longer English sentences designed to help you recognize connected speech, linking sounds, and common pronunciation changes.
The sentences are long enough to challenge your listening skills but short enough to follow through repeated practice.
This video is also useful for improving your listening comprehension for exams such as TOEIC, TOEFL, IELTS, and other English proficiency tests.
What you'll practice: - Understanding English at a natural speaking speed - Following longer English sentences - Recognizing connected speech and linking sounds - Getting used to natural English rhythm and pronunciation - Building listening confidence through repetition
You can listen while commuting, doing household chores, or working on everyday tasks.
Don't worry if you can't understand everything the first time. With regular practice, you'll gradually become more familiar with how English sounds in real conversations.
Listen every day, train your ears, and make fast English easier to understand.

ns2:group.ns2:description:
📧 Join my free AI Essentials newsletter - https://www.jeffsu.org/newsletter/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=v212

ns2:group.ns2:description:
英語は一文ずつなら聞き取れるのに、2人の会話になると急に速く感じる。そんな方のための、自然な英会話を使った対話リスニングです。
この動画では、2人の話者による実用的な英会話200をくり返し聞きながら、会話のテンポ、音のつながり、自然な英語のリズムに耳を慣らしていきます。
実際の会話では、相手の返答を聞いた直後に次の発話が始まるため、単独の英文よりも速く感じやすくなります。短い受け答えから少し長めの会話まで、難易度に変化をつけながら練習できる構成です。途中には比較的聞き取りやすい短い会話も入れているので、無理なく続けながら「今の会話は聞き取れた」という感覚も積み重ねられます。
使っている英文は、日常生活、仕事、買い物、外出、人間関係など、実際の会話で使いやすい内容が中心です。初中級〜中級レベルの方にも取り組みやすく、大学入学共通テストの短い対話問題や、英検、TOEICなどのリスニング対策にも役立ちます。
通勤中、家事中、作業中の聞き流しにもおすすめです。最初は会話が速く感じても、くり返し聞くうちに、相手の返答まで含めた「会話の流れ」が少しずつ追いやすくなってきます。

ns2:group.ns2:description:
While thousands of companies claim to sell #AI agents, only a fraction are actually building real ones.
The test is dead simple: look at what the product actually outputs:
- If it's a classification (spam or not spam), a number, or a probability, it's not generative AI. - If the output is new text, images, or video that didn't exist before, it is.
Google's own products show this perfectly:
1. Gmail's spam filter relies on classification, so it’s NOT generative AI. 2. Google Docs' "Help me write" generates brand-new text from scratch, which IS generative AI. 3. Google’s Antigravity and Anthropic’s Cowork rely on agents that can autonomously think and iterate, meaning they are actually agentic products.
Don’t be fooled by marketing speak that packages basic functions as “agentic AI.”
